correctness.rationale: For any single chord, connectivity without the chord is precisely the original cycle arc case; otherwise the chord is essential and the complement comprises exactly one contiguous gap on each internally disjoint u-v path. Both inclusions of the two-gap sumset identity were proved. Every consecutive integer interval sum lies in the (2n)x(2n) multiplication table by parity factorization. Wrapping interval sums are complements. Short-path gaps have <=1+d(d-1)/2 possible sums, long-path gaps <=1+2M(2n), and Ford’s known bound forces the claimed asymptotic. Actual code in the package exhaustively compared all 210 chord cases n=4..12 using independent methods.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 work explicitly asks how additional edges overcome incomplete cycle sums. The first general geometric no-go scale for one-chord repair gives a necessary polylogarithmic span and a stronger zero-density statement for local chords, complementing edge-count bounds and supplying a structural two-gap lemma valid for all chord positions. The result is an infinite, mathematically motivated boundary, not a recomputed finite table or arbitrary parameter slice.
